The penguins come with the palmerpenguins package.

```{r}
#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(here, tidyverse, palmerpenguins)
```

## The question

How is the data distributed? One continuous variable: `body_mass_g`, the weight of each penguin in grams. A histogram cuts the variable into intervals and counts the rows in each interval.

```{r}
#| label: look-data
penguins |>
  glimpse()
```

## 1. The first histogram

Run the chunk and read the two messages from R.

```{r}
#| label: first-histogram
penguins |>
  ggplot(aes(x = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_histogram()
```

- `using bins = 30`: R cut the weights into 30 bars. `binwidth = 200` sets the width of each bar.
- `Removed 2 rows`: 2 penguins have no body mass. `filter(!is.na(body_mass_g))` keeps the penguins with a weight.

Run the fixed version.

```{r}
#| label: fixed-histogram
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 200)
```

## 2. One histogram for all species

Fill by species. The bars stack on top of each other.

```{r}
#| label: fill-species
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = body_mass_g, fill = species)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 200)
```

`position = "identity"` draws each species from zero, one in front of the other. Adelie sits behind Chinstrap.

```{r}
#| label: position-identity
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = body_mass_g, fill = species)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 200, position = "identity")
```

`alpha = 0.5` makes the bars half transparent.

```{r}
#| label: alpha
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = body_mass_g, fill = species)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 200, position = "identity", alpha = 0.5)
```

## 3. A smooth curve

`geom_density()` draws a smooth curve. Each curve has the same area, so a species with few penguins looks as large as a species with many.

```{r}
#| label: density
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = body_mass_g, fill = species)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5)
```
